io.flic.flic2libandroid

Class Flic2Manager

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.flic.flic2libandroid.Flic2Manager

  • public class Flic2Manager
extends Object
    A manager for Flic 2 buttons.

    This class has a singleton instance that must be initialized before it can be retrieved.

    In the application's Application class, override Application.onCreate() and call init(Context, Handler), passing this as context and new Handler() as handler if you want to get all events on the main thread.

    After initialization, the singleton can betrieved using getInstance(). The utility method initAndGetInstance(Context, Handler) can be used to combine the method calls.

    To pair a new Flic 2 button, first make sure the user has the ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission. See https://developer.android.com/training/permissions/requesting for a permissions tutorial. Then call startScan(Flic2ScanCallback) and implement the callbacks.

    The manager has a SQLite database that stores all the paired buttons. If you automatically want to connect to all already paired buttons upon app boot, call getButtons() in the Application.onCreate() method of your app followed by Flic2Button.connect().

    It's recommended to register BOOT_COMPLETED and PACKAGE_REPLACED broadcast receivers in your application in order to start the app when the phone boots or the app is updated so that button connection attempts are initiated at those events.

    To keep the connections alive while an Activity is not running, you must have a Foreground Service running in your app. Otherwise the app process may be killed at any time and the Bluetooth connections are thereby terminated.

      • init

        public static void init(Context context,
                        Handler handler)
        Initializes the library.

        The handler defines what thread the library will run on. All callbacks will run on this thread. For most method calls to the library, the commands will be posted to the handler if they are invoked from another thread than the handler's thread.

        Parameters:
        context - An Android context.
        handler - The handler defines what thread the library will run on.

      • init

        public static void init(Context context,
                        HandlerInterface handler,
                        LoggerInterface logger)
        Initializes the library.

        The handler defines what thread the library will run on. All callbacks will run on this thread. For most method calls to the library, the commands will be posted to the handler if they are invoked from another thread than the handler's thread.

        This method takes a custom handler type and should only be used if you have a different thread scheduler.

        Parameters:
        context - An Android context.
        handler - The handler defines what thread the library will run on.
        logger - A logger for debug purposes, can be null.

      • errorCodeToString

        public static String errorCodeToString(int code)
        Converts an error code to a string representation.

        This is either a result code passed to the scan callback Flic2ScanCallback.onComplete(int, int, Flic2Button) or a failure code passed to the callback Flic2ButtonListener.onFailure(Flic2Button, int, int).

        Parameters:

        a non-null string

      • startScan

        public void startScan(Flic2ScanCallback flic2ScanCallback)
        Starts a button scan.

        This starts a scan for Flic 2 buttons. Please ask the user for ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION first (see https://developer.android.com/training/permissions/requesting).

        The progress will be published through the callback.

        If there already is a scan ongoing, the callback is invoked with Flic2ScanCallback.RESULT_FAILED_ALREADY_RUNNING.

        Parameters:
        flic2ScanCallback - callback object
        Throws:
        SecurityException - if ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is not granted before this call

      • stopScan

        public void stopScan()
        Stops the currently running scan.

        Assuming this method is called from the same thread as the handler's thread, the pairing attempt is immediately aborted and the Flic2ScanCallback.onComplete(int, int, Flic2Button) callback will NOT be called.

      • forgetButton

        public void forgetButton(Flic2Button button)
        Forgets a paired button.

        Removes a button from the list of paired buttons. If it's in the connected state, it is disconnected.

        If this button already is removed, this method does nothing.

        If the button was connected, Flic2ButtonListener.onDisconnect(Flic2Button) will be called. In any case, Flic2ButtonListener.onUnpaired(Flic2Button) will finally be called.

        From now on Flic2Button.connect() will do nothing.

        Parameters:
        button - the button to forget
